body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-17 while verifying #1685. Running `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` leaves an
untracked `annotation-backups/` directory in the repository root containing real gzipped snapshot
files.

Cause: `cps/services/annotation_backup.py:82` resolves the backup root as
`Path(constants.CONFIG_DIR) / "annotation-backups"`, and under some test contexts CONFIG_DIR
resolves to the current working directory rather than a temporary one.

NOT introduced by #1685 — the directory predates that branch. It is also NOT in `.gitignore`, so it
shows up as untracked for anyone who runs the suite, and a careless `git add -A` would commit
gzipped annotation payloads.

Neither `tests/unit/test_annotation_backup.py` nor `tests/unit/test_kobo_annotation_stage0.py`
produces it in isolation, so the writer is some other test that reaches the backup path with the
default CONFIG_DIR. Finding that caller is step one.

Two fixes, the second being the real one:
1. Add `annotation-backups/` to `.gitignore` so it can never be committed by accident.
2. Point CONFIG_DIR at a tmpdir in the test context, so the suite stops writing outside its own
   scratch space at all.
title: Unit tests write annotation-backups/ into the repo root
